messages.author: ab7b24da45678eac
messages.subject: Re: R parallel instructions?
parts:
I would be happy to do that.  But could I ask for what is this instruction for in particular so that I would have a better idea. 

For running in parallel in R, we only provide sflist2stanfit to combine results from run stan() in parallel.  In particular, see the notes and examples in the doc of sflist2stanfit.  So we do not care how the parallelism is done using whatever package, on clusters, or just one box.  In the example of sflis2stanfit, only an example using package parallel is given. 

> ?sflist2stanfit

For extract, the doc of extract and as.array.stanfit give a lot of details and examples.  
> ?extract
> ?as.array.stanfit 


--
Jiqiang

To be clear, it is not a function to do parallel sampling.  It just combines results 
from runs of stan() regardless of they are executed in parallel or not. 

In addition, I had added a couple of lines using extract in the getting started wiki page 
and the doc of stan(). 

I think one issue for doc or tutorial is that people do not know where to begin with. 
For us, I suppose it is just to write it everywhere.  I guess I can more about parallel 
stuff to the getting started wiki page and the vignettes. 

I am not a big fan about R as I started programming from C.  My way to deal with it
is to learn the least of R that is needed for me.  For ggplot, I just mimic examples from internet
to accomplish my goal. 

--

messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Re: R parallel instructions?
parts:
There are code snippets by me and Sebastian Webber on this thread

https://groups.google.com/d/topic/stan-users/3goteHAsJGs/discussion

The main obstacle is that there are no universal instructions for doing things in parallel. For !Windows and local, using mclapply() in the parallel package is the best.

But no matter what anyone is doing, basically you just call stan() in parallel and use sflist2stanfit() to merge the result into one stanfit object.

Ben
